facts.text: Kimberton grew around Chrisman's tavern and mill, which opened in 1796 and later became the town’s post office until 1938.
In 1817 Emmor Kimber arrived, quickly establishing himself as the community’s leading citizen and a prominent county figure.
After the Civil War, the post‑Civil War railroad station sparked a boom, turning Kimberton into an agricultural depot that shipped produce to Phoenixville and Philadelphia.
In 1775 the Continental Congress chose a site along French Creek near Kimberton for the Continental Powder Mill, which supplied gunpowder to the Revolutionary Army.
The Kimberton Village Historic District was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1976, with a boundary increase in 1987.
The East Pikeland Historical Commission has stabilized the old mill and is working to promote the site as a heritage tourism destination.
